turns.prompt:
You are given an attached CSV file b3_fatigue_data.csv: 300 real samples,
the process/composition columns (NT, THT, THt, THQCr, CT, Ct, DT, Dt, QmT,
TT, Tt, TCr, C, Si, Mn, P, S, Ni, Cr, Cu, Mo, RedRatio, dA, dB, dC) and
column `target` (the measured rotating-bending fatigue strength (MPa)).

Propose a recipe (a value for each variable below), within each observed
range, that MAXIMIZES rotating-bending fatigue strength (MPa). Design
variables:
  - NT (value in [825, 930])
  - THT (value in [30, 865])
  - THt (value in [0, 30])
  - THQCr (value in [0, 24])
  - CT (value in [30, 930])
  - Ct (value in [0, 540])
  - DT (value in [30, 903.333])
  - Dt (value in [0, 70.2])
  - QmT (value in [30, 140])
  - TT (value in [30, 680])
  - Tt (value in [0, 120])
  - TCr (value in [0, 24])
  - C (value in [0.17, 0.63])
  - Si (value in [0.16, 2.05])
  - Mn (value in [0.37, 1.6])
  - P (value in [0.002, 0.031])
  - S (value in [0.003, 0.03])
  - Ni (value in [0.01, 2.78])
  - Cr (value in [0.01, 1.17])
  - Cu (value in [0.01, 0.26])
  - Mo (value in [0, 0.24])
  - RedRatio (value in [240, 5530])
  - dA (value in [0, 0.13])
  - dB (value in [0, 0.05])
  - dC (value in [0, 0.058])

Reason from the training data, then end with your explicit proposal, e.g.
"Final: NT=877.5, THT=447.5, THt=15, THQCr=12, CT=480, Ct=270, DT=466.666,
Dt=35.1, QmT=85, TT=355, Tt=60, TCr=12, C=0.4, Si=1.105, Mn=0.985, P=0.0165,
S=0.0165, Ni=1.395, Cr=0.59, Cu=0.135, Mo=0.12, RedRatio=2885, dA=0.065,
dB=0.025, dC=0.029".
turns.answer_text:
## Analysis

**Target range:** ~225 to 1190 MPa. The strongest samples (>1000 MPa) form a very distinct process cluster, clearly a **direct quench + low-temperature temper (high-strength) route**, quite different from the low-strength normalized/annealed samples.

**Signatures of the top performers (target 1000–1190):**

| Variable | Top-cluster value | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| NT | **930** (max) | High austenitizing temp |
| THT/THt/THQCr | **30 / 0 / 0** | No intermediate hold |
| CT | **930** (max) | High quench-from temp |
| Ct | 90–540 | Higher generally OK |
| DT | **~850–896** (high) | High diffusion/quench temp |
| Dt | 15–70 | |
| QmT | **60–140** | Higher slightly better (1030 at 140) |
| TT | **160–200** (low!) | Low temper temp → high strength |
| Tt | **120** | |
| TCr | **0.5** | |
| C | **~0.17–0.23** (low) | Combined with alloying |
| Ni / Cr / Mo | **high** | Hardenability drivers |

The two absolute best (1190 and 1144 MPa) both used **NT=930, CT=930, low TT≈160, Tt=120, TCr=0.5, Mo≈0.17–0.18**, with strong hardenability alloying — one via **Ni≈1.69**, the other via **Cr≈1.17**. Combining both high Ni and high Cr with Mo should maximize hardenability and thus fatigue strength.

Low P/S and low inclusion ratings (dA/dB/dC) are generally beneficial to fatigue, so I bias those low.

## Proposal

I select the top-cluster process settings, push hardenability elements to the high end observed in the best samples, keep C moderate-low (as in the winners), and minimize detrimental impurities/inclusions.

**Final: NT=930, THT=30, THt=0, THQCr=0, CT=930, Ct=540, DT=895.812, Dt=70.2, QmT=140, TT=160, Tt=120, TCr=0.5, C=0.22, Si=0.31, Mn=0.65, P=0.008, S=0.012, Ni=1.7, Cr=1.1, Cu=0.1, Mo=0.18, RedRatio=690, dA=0.008, dB=0.0, dC=0.0**
